This integration connects Gladys to **your Wiser by Feller µGateway** through
its **official local API**, and offers the outputs of your installation in the
**Discovery** tab of Gladys: lights, dimmers, switched outlets, venetian
blinds, shutters and awnings, as well as your **Wiser scenes** and the
**presses of the buttons** registered on the µGateway. Once a device is added,
its state follows the µGateway **live**, and Gladys controls it through it.
Everything stays on your local network: no cloud. Unofficial, not affiliated
with Feller AG.

> **Development version (0.1).** Written from Feller's API documentation and
> the aiowiserbyfeller library, and tested against a simulated µGateway: it
> has never been tested with a real µGateway yet. Feedback is welcome on the
> GitHub repository.

## What you get

| Wiser output                      | In Gladys                                                                             |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Switch (light)                    | a light: on/off                                                                       |
| Dimmer (LED, DALI)                | a light: on/off and brightness (0-100 %)                                              |
| Switch set as "outlet" in the app | a switch: on/off                                                                      |
| Venetian blind                    | a shutter: open, close, stop, position; the **slats** as their own device, on request |
| Roller shutter, motor             | a shutter: open, close, stop, position                                                |
| Awning                            | a curtain: open, close, stop, position                                                |
| Plain relay motor                 | a shutter: open, close, stop (no position)                                            |
| Impulse or staircase-timer output | a read-only state and an "Activate" button, **off by default**                        |
| Wiser scene                       | a "Run" button: the scene runs as from the app                                        |
| Button registered on the µGateway | a button: every press reaches your Gladys scenes                                      |

Blinds and shutters are **never** switches: a "turn everything off" scene does
not close them. The position follows the Gladys convention: 100 % = open, 0 %
= closed. While a motor learns its end positions (calibration), its position
is unknown and not sent.

An on/off output is a light or a switch only when it has **no sub-type at
all**: an output set as impulse, timer or with any other sub-type becomes an
impulse output (read-only, its button behind the option). If you set an output
as impulse **after** adding it (in the eSetup app), click **Scan** in the
Discovery tab, then **delete the device and add it again**: its old light
commands are refused until then.

A **Wiser scene** that drives an impulse output is guarded like it: refused
while the option is off (read again just before sending), and at least 3
seconds between two impulses of the same output, whether they come from the
scene or from the "Activate" button. A scene that runs scripts is guarded the
same way as soon as an impulse output exists.

Devices are named after the output and its room in the Wiser app ("Ceiling
(Living room)"). Their id follows the physical address of the output (module
and channel): it does not change if the µGateway renumbers its outputs. HVAC
outputs, and the colours and white temperature of DALI lights, are not
controlled yet.

### Buttons and scene triggers

The µGateway (generation B, firmware 6.0.41 or later) sends the presses of the
**registered** ("managed") buttons over its WebSocket. Each registered button
becomes a Gladys device whose "Press" feature takes one value per press: short
press, long press, release, telling up/down and on/off apart on a rocker. Use
it as a "Device state change" trigger in a scene. Two presses in a row are two
events. Gladys does not register buttons itself (that would change the
configuration of the µGateway): register them through the API of the µGateway
(`POST /api/buttons`) or a tool that does it, then click **Scan** in the
Discovery tab. Generation A µGateways do not send these presses.

## Requirements

- A Wiser by Feller µGateway on the same local network as Gladys, and its IP
  address (preferably fixed, reserved in your router).
- Physical access to the µGateway to press one of its buttons once, when
  getting the token.

## Setup

1. In Gladys, open the **Wiser by Feller** integration, **Configuration** tab.
2. Type the **IP address** of the µGateway (like `192.168.1.20`) and save.
3. Click **Get the token**. The buttons of the µGateway blink for 30 seconds:
   **press one of them**. The token is saved in the "Token of the µGateway"
   field by itself and Gladys connects.
4. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the devices you want.

The button sends **one request per click**, never in a loop. Without a press
within 30 s nothing changes: click again. Each new token replaces the previous
one (the µGateway invalidates the old one).

The token of the "gladys" account starts as a copy of the Wiser account chosen
in "Wiser account to copy" (`admin`, the one of the Wiser Home app, by
default): names, rooms and scenes come from it.

## Options

- **Live updates** (on by default): Gladys listens to the WebSocket of the
  µGateway; the states follow within a second and the button presses arrive.
  The states are also read every 5 minutes, and the list of outputs, scenes
  and buttons every 30 minutes (or with **Scan** in the Discovery tab).
- **Read interval** (30 s by default, 10 to 3600 s): without the live updates
  (off or lost), the states are read at this pace.
- **Allow impulse and timer outputs** (off by default): an "impulse" or
  "staircase timer" output often drives a garage door opener or a door
  strike. While the option is off, its "Activate" button is refused, and the
  option is read again just before each request. Two impulses are at least 3
  seconds apart.
- **Slats of venetian blinds as their own device** (off by default): each
  venetian blind also offers a "\<blind> – Slats" device (0-100 %). Beware: a
  "close all blinds" of Google, Alexa, HomeKit or an assistant (MCP) may
  target this device too.
- **Language of the feature names**: French or English.

If the WebSocket says nothing for 10 minutes, Gladys opens it again (a
µGateway that drops it silently); in a quiet house this only costs a
reconnection. A socket that opens then drops at once keeps a growing retry
delay (up to 2 minutes), and the states are never read more than once per
interval.

## Security and privacy

- The token is **kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, and sent
  only to the address typed** (in the `Authorization` header). It never
  appears in the logs. Redirections are never followed.
- A token refused by the µGateway is **never tried again automatically**, even
  after a restart: Gladys waits for you to get a new token or click **Test the
  connection**.
- A "429" of the µGateway pauses everything (1 minute to 6 hours).
- Commands leave one at a time per output, within 3.5 s, or are refused. A
  command that may have left without an answer (a 5xx, an answer not
  understood, a timeout once sent) is told "sent, without confirmation" and
  the output is read again; a refusal of the µGateway (4xx) is told
  "refused"; a µGateway unreachable before sending gives "not sent".

## Troubleshooting

- **"The µGateway refused the token"**: click **Get the token** and press a
  button of the µGateway.
- **"Unreachable"**: check the IP address (no `.local` name, the container does
  not resolve them) and that the µGateway is powered.
- **No live updates**: the states are read at the chosen interval; the badge of
  the device shows it with an orange dot.
- **Test the connection** shows the model, the firmware, the number of
  outputs, scenes and registered buttons, and the state of the live updates.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt Wiser by Feller in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Wiser by Feller installation in Gladys | `section` | Nein | The outputs of your Wiser µGateway are offered in the Discovery tab: lights (on/off, brightness), switched outlets, blinds and shutters (position; slats of venetian blinds on request), awnings, your Wiser scenes as buttons, and the presses of the buttons registered on the µGateway. Everything stays on your local network, through the official API of the µGateway, with live updates. Impulse and staircase-timer outputs stay read-only until you allow them below. Never tested with a real µGateway yet. Unofficial, not affiliated with Feller AG. |
| Address of the µGateway | `string` | Ja | The local IP address of your Wiser µGateway, like 192.168.1.20 (shown in the Wiser Home app, or in your router). The token is sent to this address only. |
| Token of the µGateway | `secret` | Nein | Filled in by the "Get the token" button below: save the address first, click the button, then press any button of the µGateway within 30 seconds while they blink. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, and sent only to the address above. |
| Wiser account to copy | `select` | Nein | Names, rooms and scenes belong to a Wiser account: the token of Gladys starts as a copy of this one when you get it. "admin" is the account of the Wiser Home app. |
| Live updates | `boolean` | Nein | Listens to the WebSocket of the µGateway: the states follow within a second and the button presses reach your scenes. Off: the states are read at the interval below and the presses are not seen. |
| Read interval without live updates (s) | `number` | Nein | How often the states are read when the live updates are off or lost (10 to 3600 s). With them, every 5 minutes. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | Nein | Used for the names of the features of the devices added from now on. |
| Allow impulse and timer outputs | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: impulse and staircase-timer outputs (a garage door opener is often wired to one) are read-only. On, their "Activate" button sends a press, from the dashboard and the scenes. |
| Slats of venetian blinds as their own device | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default. On, each venetian blind also offers a "\<blind> – Slats" device in Discovery. Beware: a "close all blinds" of Google, Alexa, HomeKit or an assistant (MCP) may target it too. |

## So installierst du Wiser by Feller in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Wiser by Feller erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-wiser-feller:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-wiser-feller](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-wiser-feller).

Wiser by Feller benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Wiser by Feller ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
